name: つじ田 日本橋八重洲店
address_ja: 東京都中央区八重洲1-4-6 八重洲境井ビル 1F
cuisine: Sixteen counter seats of the thick pork-bone-and-seafood tsukemen that made つじ田 famous — you eat the noodles plain, then with sudachi, then with Kyoto black shichimi, and finish with soup-wari; bowls come in under ¥1,000
neighborhood: Yaesu 1-chōme, on the Yaesu-dōri side of Tokyo Station — 3 min from Nihonbashi (Ginza / Tōzai lines, exit A7), 5 min from Tokyo Station's Yaesu north exit
gf_detail: Not workable for anyone avoiding gluten. The dish is wheat noodles — two custom flours co-developed with 三河屋製麺 — and the dipping broth is a pork/chicken/fish/kombu reduction finished with ordinary wheat soy sauce. The group's own allergen page carries a blanket cross-contact statement: 「各メニューの調理には同じ調理器具を使用しているため、本来その商品に使用しない食材が調理時に付着・混入する可能性があります」 and 「麺、スープ等の製造工場では、小麻、卵、乳成分を原材料とする商品の製造を行ってます」. No gluten-free item is offered and none is claimed.
vegan_detail: The house broth is built on pork bones, chicken carcass and seafood — 「厳選の豚骨、鶏がら、魚介、昆布、野菜、他合計十数種類の食材」 — and the standard bowl comes with chashu and a marinated egg. There is no vegetarian or vegan option on the menu.

roles: つじ田 group branch (corporate site: oishes.com)
chef_bio.background: つじ田 opened in Kanda-Ochanomizu in 2005 — 「2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来」 — and became one of the shops that defined the Tokyo nōkō gyokai tsukemen style. The house does not publish a chef's name; the brand's identity is the method rather than a personality. The broth is a reduction of 「厳選の豚骨、鶏がら、魚介、昆布、野菜、他合計十数種類の食材」; the noodles are two bespoke types made with 三河屋製麺, one cut for tsukemen and one for ramen. The shop prescribes a three-stage 「つけ麺流儀」: the first third of the noodles plain, sudachi squeezed over the second third, and a Kyoto kuro-shichimi from a spice house founded in 1704 on the last third, then soup-wari to drink the broth down. This Yaesu branch opened on 10 July 2013 and is a 16-seat counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: One dish done to a fixed ritual: a rich pork-and-fish dip, sharpened first with citrus and then with pepper, so the same bowl tastes like three.
chef_bio.specialty: 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 with sudachi and 黒七味; 味噂 and dandan variants exist at other group brands, not here.

anecdotes.text: The shop's own こだわり page sets out the eating order as a rule rather than a suggestion — plain noodles, then sudachi at the one-third mark, then 黒七味 for the last third, then スープ割り.
The 黒七味 is bought in from a Kyoto spice house the shop dates to 1704, so the last few mouthfuls taste of Gion rather than of Tokyo.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog's entry for つじ田 日本橋八重洲店 gives the address 中央区八重洲1-4-6 八重洲境井ビル1F, coordinates, 16 counter seats, the 11:00-22:30 weekday / 11:00-21:00 weekend hours with 不定休, a sub-¥1,000 budget band both sittings, all-non-smoking, and an opening date of 10 July 2013. The brand site supplies the 2005 Kanda-Ochanomizu origin, the broth composition, the 三河屋製麼 noodles and the three-stage eating method. The group allergen page supplies the shared-utensil and wheat/egg/dairy factory statements.

gf_cross_contamination.text: 「各メニューの調理には同じ調理器具を使用しているため、本来その商品に使用しない食材が調理時に付着・混入する可能性があります」 — the operator's own words. A 16-seat noodle counter boils wheat noodles in one pot all day.
「麼、スープ等の製造工場では、小麻、卵、乳成分を原材料とする商品の製造を行ってます」 — wheat is present upstream at the factory as well as in the shop.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No gluten-free tamari is named anywhere; the tare is assumed to be ordinary wheat shōyu.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork bone, chicken carcass and fish are the base of the only broth in the shop.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The group publishes a per-brand allergen PDF and a contact form, so a specific ingredient question can be answered in writing before you go — but it is disclosure, not accommodation.

cultural_comfort.note: A 16-seat all-counter noodle bar in a Yaesu office block, three minutes from Nihonbashi station's A7 exit. Open straight through from 11:00, no reservations, cash or Suica (no credit cards), and you will be in and out in twenty minutes. Queues at peak lunch. English is not guaranteed but the ordering is point-and-pay and the shop posts the eating method in pictures. Not a place to negotiate a special preparation.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「つけ麼 つじ田」 with a Yaesu centroid pin; the business is つじ田 日本橋八重洲店 at 中央区八重洲1-4-6 八重洲境井ビル1F, confirmed on Tabelog (address, 16 counter seats, hours, 2013-07-10 opening) and consistent with the brand's own site. Coordinates replaced with the real address's, loc_precise:true — the sweep's pin was about 150 m off.

name: 築地寿司清 築地本店
cuisine: Edomae sushi counter trading since 1889, now buying at Toyosu — nigiri ¥220-660 a piece, set courses 和 ¥1,850 / 匠 ¥3,500 / おまかせ ¥4,500 / おまかせ‐極‐ ¥6,000, and a 大名ちらし at ¥2,500 for lunch
neighborhood: Tsukiji 4-chōme on the far side of Harumi-dōri from the old market — 3 min from Tsukiji-shijō (Toei Ōedo line), 5 min from Tsukiji (Hibiya line); Shintomichō (Yūrakuchō line) is about 10 min north
gf_detail: Nothing gluten-free is claimed and no tamari is named, so assume the nikiri brushed on the nigiri and the soy at the counter are both wheat shōyu — the default in Japan. Plain nigiri and sashimi are the workable part of this menu; the published 一品料理 list is not (いかげそ焼, 鯰がり巻, 貝串焼 辛味噌添え all sit on wheat-based seasonings, and tamagoyaki in an Edomae shop normally carries flour). The tare on anago is a wheat-soy reduction. A celiac would have to bring their own tamari, order nigiri only, and say so at the counter; the shop has published no allergen policy either way. Rated 'ask' rather than 'options' because the evidence is silence, not accommodation.
vegan_detail: An Edomae sushi counter. The menu is fish end to end — nigiri, sashimi platters, anago, shiokara, mixed-shellfish plates — with no vegetable or inari set published, and the rice seasoning and any dashi will not be animal-free. Nothing on the site suggests a vegetarian arrangement is available.

roles: 株式会社築地寿司清 (TSUKIJISUSHISAY CO., LTD.) — flagship branch
chef_bio.background: 築地寿司清 dates itself to 明治22年 — 1889 — and describes 130-odd years of Edomae practice: 「明治２２年の創業以来、守り継いできた伝統と技が磨き上げた江戸前寿司の粲をお届けします」. The house line is deliberately unstarry: 「豊洲市場の厳選した素材で、130余年の歴史で培ってきた『本物の江戸前寿司』をより多くの方に気軽に召し上がっていただきたい」 — real Edomae, priced so people actually eat it. No individual itamae is named publicly; the company now runs some three dozen counters and department-store branches from Hakata to Niigata, but this Tsukiji 4-chōme address is the original house, with a 16-seat counter downstairs and a second counter and tables upstairs. Since the market moved in 2018 the fish comes from Toyosu, a fact the company states on its own front page rather than hiding.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「味」、「新鮮」、「丁寧」 — taste, freshness, care — with the buying done by the house's own professional eye and the price kept where a neighbourhood can reach it.
chef_bio.specialty: Nigiri to order at ¥220-660 a piece; the counter-only おまかせ-極- (¥6,000) and おまかせ (¥4,500, 12 pieces); 大名ちらし ¥2,500 at lunch; house shiokara at ¥600 and anago shirayaki at ¥1,800.

anecdotes.text: The shop takes reservations only from 17:00 and only for a limited number of seats — 「17：00～予約可（予約席数に制限あり）」 — so daytime is walk-in.

Wednesday is the closing day, inherited from the old Tsukiji market's own 休市日 rhythm; the company's news page occasionally announces trading on a Wednesday when the sister 新館 is shut for building work.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The company site's 築地本店 page gives the address 〒104-0045 中央区築地4-13-9, phone 03-3541-7720, the full priced menu, the weekday and weekend hours with last entry 19:30, Wednesday closing, 16 counter seats on the first floor plus 10 counter and 8 table seats on the second, all-non-smoking, and average spends of ¥2,500 at lunch and ¥4,000 at dinner. Tabelog corroborates the address and the 1889 opening year and puts the coordinates at 35.664832 / 139.770451. The corporate front page supplies the 明治22年 founding and the Toyosu sourcing.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No wheat-free handling is claimed. Tamagoyaki, anago tare and the fried/simmered ippin dishes all sit in the same service as the nigiri, and the counter's shared soy dish is wheat shōyu.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat shōyu assumed throughout — the nikiri brushed on Edomae nigiri is a soy reduction and no gluten-free tamari is mentioned anywhere on the site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The entire published menu is fish and shellfish; there is no vegetable course.

positives.text: Nigiri is sold by the piece (¥220-660), so a diner avoiding a specific ingredient can build a meal item by item rather than accept a fixed course.

cultural_comfort.note: An old, plainly-signed sushi house rather than a tourist counter, but an easy one: it opens at 10:00, takes cards and IC/phone payment, and has a printed picture-and-price menu including ¥1,850 and ¥2,500 sets, so you can order without negotiating. Sit at a second-floor table if you would rather not talk to an itamae; the ground-floor counter is where the conversation happens. Closed Wednesdays. Reservations only from 17:00, by phone in Japanese.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「寿司清」, which is a short form rather than a trading name; the business in Tsukiji is 築地寿司清, and the address closest to the sweep's pin is the 1889 original, 築地寿司清 築地本店 at 中央区築地4-13-9. Confidence is 'medium' only because the record named no branch and the company's sister counter 築地新館 stands 60 m away at 築地4-13-5 (35.665254 / 139.770915, 70 seats, later hours, its own Tabelog entry) — if the sweep meant that one, the coordinates move by less than 100 m. Note also that the record's 「新富町駅」 label is wrong for either: both are 3-5 min from Tsukiji-shijō / Tsukiji, roughly 10 min from Shintomichō. Coordinates replaced with 築地本店's, loc_precise:true.

name: 築地玉寿司 築地本店
cuisine: The 1924 original of the Tamazushi chain — a 35-seat Edomae sushi house one minute from Tsukiji station, doing kaisen-don and sets around ¥1,000-2,000 at lunch and ¥5,000-6,000 in the evening, with a counter course cut by a chef in front of you
neighborhood: Tsukiji 1-chōme, at the top of the Tsukiji block toward Shintomichō — 1 min from Tsukiji (Hibiya line, exit 4), 2 min from Shintomichō (Yūrakuchō line), 3 min from Higashi-Ginza
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim and no tamari named, so assume wheat shōyu throughout — both the dish at the table and the nikiri brushed on Edomae nigiri. Straight nigiri and sashimi are the workable part; the shop is also an izakaya by genre, so a fryer and wheat-seasoned small plates are in the same kitchen, and the anago tare and tamagoyaki should be treated as wheat. Nothing published addresses allergens either way, hence 'ask' — bring your own tamari and raise it before the itamae starts.
vegan_detail: Edomae sushi, kaisen-don and izakaya plates — fish throughout, with no vegetarian set published. Kanpyō-maki and kappa-maki would be the only fallbacks and even those come from a board handling fish; nothing on the company's site offers a vegetable course.

roles: 株式会社築地玉寿司 — founding branch
chef_bio.background: 築地玉寿司 opened in 大正13年 (1924), the year after the Great Kantō Earthquake, and describes its own beginning as 「一枚の暉簾（のれん）から玉寿司の物語は始まりました」 — the story began with a single noren. A century on it runs eighteen locations across the Kantō region plus Sapporo and Nagoya, but Tsukiji 1-9-4 is the house that started it, and it is small: 35 seats, 22 at tables and 13 at the counter. The company's self-description is domestic rather than gastronomic — 「大正からの歴史が繋ぐ、家族全員が安心できる場所」, a place the whole family can be comfortable — and alongside the counter courses it sells sushi-making experiences and takeout. No individual chef is named publicly. Its price bands are unusually wide for Tsukiji: a ¥1,000-2,000 lunch and a ¥5,000-6,000 dinner in the same room.
chef_bio.philosophy: A hundred years of Edomae technique deliberately kept approachable — counters where a family, a tourist and a regular can all sit down without a referral.
chef_bio.specialty: Edomae nigiri cut to order at the counter; kaisen-don and sushi sets at lunch; sushi-making experience sessions run by the company.

anecdotes.text: The company dates itself to a single noren curtain hung in Taishō 13 — 「一枚の暉簾（のれん）から玉寿司の物語は始まりました」 — and now runs five separate brands from it.
Unusually for an old Tsukiji sushi house, it trades every day of the year except the New Year holiday, and straight through lunch and dinner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog gives 築地玉寿司 築地本店 at 中央区築地1-9-4, coordinates 35.669309 / 139.771739, genre 寿司・海鮮丈・居酒屋, 35 seats (22 tables + 13 counter), 11:00-15:00 and 17:00-22:00 daily with no closing day except the New Year, budget ¥5,000-5,999 evening and ¥1,000-1,999 lunch, all-non-smoking, cards accepted, opened 1924, and one-minute access from Tsukiji station. The company site confirms the Taishō founding, the same address, the same hours, the two-minute walk from Tsukiji exit 4, and the eighteen-location footprint.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Genre is 寿司・海鮮丈・居酒屋 — an izakaya menu runs alongside the sushi, so fried and wheat-seasoned dishes share the kitchen. No wheat-free handling is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No gluten-free tamari is mentioned anywhere on the company site; assume wheat shōyu in the dish, in the nikiri and in the anago tare.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish and shellfish throughout; no vegetarian set is published.

positives.text: A large, everyday, all-day counter with printed sets at ¥1,000-2,000 — easy to walk into and easy to order from item by item, which is what a restricted diner needs more than a special menu.

cultural_comfort.note: Probably the least intimidating serious sushi counter in Tsukiji: one minute from the station's exit 4, open 11:00-15:00 and 17:00-22:00 every day but New Year, cards accepted, tables as well as a counter, and a chain's worth of printed menus and photographs. Lunch sets in the ¥1,000-2,000 band mean you do not have to guess at a bill. Tourists are normal here; the company also sells sushi-making sessions, so questions from foreigners are routine rather than awkward.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION (branch only). The light record read 「築地玉寿司」, which is the chain name; the business at the record's Tsukiji pin is the founding branch, 築地玉寿司 築地本店 at 中央区築地1-9-4, confirmed on both Tabelog and the company's own site (address, 1924 opening, 35 seats, daily 11:00-15:00 / 17:00-22:00). One caution for the merge: the chain has a second Tsukiji branch, 築地玉寿司 晴海通り店, 250 m from Tsukiji station, so a duplicate could enter the dataset from a later sweep. name: 寿司大
address_ja: 東京都江東区豊洲6-5-1 豊洲市場 6街区 水産仲卸売場棟 3F
cuisine: The fish-market omakase pilgrimage — a 16-seat counter inside Toyosu's wholesale block serving one set course of the morning's tuna and shellfish, plus a final piece of your choosing, in the ¥5,000-6,000 band, from 6am until the fish runs out
neighborhood: Toyosu Market, block 6, third floor of the seafood intermediate-wholesale building — 3 min from Shijō-mae on the Yurikamome (344 m); no longer in Tsukiji
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金・土 06:00 - 14:00／日・祝日 定休日　定休日：休市日（原則水曜日）
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim, no tamari named, and no menu you can edit — this is a fixed omakase in which the itamae brushes each piece with nikiri, a wheat-soy reduction, before it reaches you. Tamagoyaki closes the course in most market counters and normally carries flour. If you need wheat-free you would have to say so before the first piece, in Japanese, at a counter with a queue behind you and no printed allergen information; nothing published suggests they can or will adapt. Rated 'ask' because the ingredients are mostly rice and raw fish and the barrier is the seasoning, not the dish — but treat it as unresolved rather than workable.
vegan_detail: A tuna-market sushi counter running a single fixed course. There is no vegetarian option and no à la carte to retreat to.

roles: market sushi counter, Toyosu wholesale block 6
chef_bio.origin: Tsukiji inner market — 中央区築地5-2-1 — until the 2018 move
chef_bio.background: 寿司大 was one of the two or three counters that made queueing inside the Tsukiji inner market a tourist ritual, and it carried the ritual across the water: Tabelog records the shop as having moved from 中央区築地5-2-1 and reopening at Toyosu in September 2018. It is tiny — fourteen counter seats and one table for two to four — which is the whole reason for the queue, not a detail of it. Trading hours run 06:00 to 14:00 on market days, closed Sundays, holidays and the market's own closed days (usually Wednesday). Cash only: no cards, no electronic money, no QR. The house does not publish a chef's name or a written philosophy; it publishes a queue and a set course, and the price band sits at ¥5,000-5,999. What it does keep is an X account, @sushidai_toyosu, which is where opening changes are announced.
chef_bio.philosophy: Not stated by the shop. In practice: one course, whatever the market had that morning, cut in front of fourteen people at a time.
chef_bio.specialty: The set omakase course, finished with a piece of the diner's own choosing; tuna in its three grades from the market downstairs.

anecdotes.text: Tabelog lists the shop's opening date at Toyosu as September 2018 and records the previous address as 中央区築地5-2-1, with the old pre-move listing kept separately — the clearest documentary trace of the market's relocation.
Cash only, in a building where the shops around it take PayPay — a deliberate holdover from the inner market.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog gives 寿司大 (スシダイ) at 江東区豊洲6-5-1 豊洲市場 内6街区 水産仲卸売場棟3F, coordinates 35.644310 / 139.782461, 344 m from Shijō-mae on the Yurikamome, 16 seats (14 counter plus one table), 06:00-14:00 Monday to Saturday with Sundays, holidays and 休市日 closed, budget ¥5,000-5,999, no cashless payment of any kind, all-non-smoking, opened September 2018, official account https://x.com/sushidai_toyosu, and the explicit note 「このお店は「中央区築地5-2-1」から移転しています」.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A fixed omakase with no written allergen information, in a market counter that runs one service for everyone. Nothing wheat-free is claimed or offered.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Edomae nigiri is brushed with nikiri — a wheat soy-sauce reduction — by the chef before it is handed over; no tamari is named.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A tuna-market counter serving one fish course; there is no vegetarian alternative.

cultural_comfort.note: Hard on logistics, not on manners. You are inside a working wholesale market: get to Shijō-mae on the Yurikamome early, check the market calendar because Wednesdays are usually closed, and expect a long standing queue for fourteen seats. Bring cash — no cards, no IC, no QR. There is no menu to read: you sit, the course comes, and at the end you name one last piece, which is the only moment you need any Japanese. Tourists are entirely normal here, but the pace is brisk and there is nowhere to linger.

enrich_note: RELOCATED, NOT MISLOCATED. 寿司大 is real and open, but it has not been in Tsukiji since 2018: Tabelog states 「このお店は「中央区築地5-2-1」から移転しています」 and gives the current address as 江東区豊洲6-5-1, inside Toyosu Market's block 6, open since September 2018. The light record's 中央区築地 pin was therefore about 9 km out; coordinates have been replaced with the Toyosu ones and loc_precise set true. This is still Tokyo, so it is not a MISLOCATED RECORD in the brief's sense — but a human should decide whether a Toyosu-market shop belongs in a Tsukiji-labelled tranche, since the neighbourhood string the sweep attached to it is now wrong.

neighborhood: Toyosu Market, block 5, ground floor of the fruit-and-vegetable building — 3 min from Shijō-mae on the Yurikamome (112 m); no longer in Tsukiji
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金・土 06:00 - 13:00／日・祝日 定休日　定休日：市場閉市日
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim and no tamari named. As at any Edomae counter the nikiri brushed on each piece is a wheat soy-sauce reduction, and the tamagoyaki that closes a market course normally contains flour. The raw material is rice and fish, so the barrier is the seasoning rather than the dish, but nothing published shows the shop can serve a wheat-free version and there is no written allergen information. roles: market sushi counter, Toyosu wholesale block 5
chef_bio.origin: Tsukiji inner market — 中央区築地5-2-1 — until the 2018 move
chef_bio.background: 大和寿司 spent decades as one of the two counters people queued for inside the Tsukiji inner market, and it reopened at Toyosu on 13 October 2018; Tabelog records the move from 中央区築地5-2-1 in as many words and notes 「築地場内市場の大和寿司が豊洲市場に移転」. The new room is larger than the old stall — 26 seats, counter only — and sits on the ground floor of the produce building rather than among the fish, 112 m from Shijō-mae station. Trading is 06:00 to 13:00 on market days, closed Sundays, holidays and 市場閉市日. Unlike its neighbour 寿司大 it takes cards, transport IC, iD and PayPay. The budget band is ¥6,000-7,999. No chef is named publicly and the shop keeps no website.
chef_bio.philosophy: Not stated by the shop. In practice: a market breakfast omakase, cut fast, at a wide counter, for people who came in on the first train.
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase nigiri of the morning's market fish; tuna in grades from the wholesalers a hundred metres away.

anecdotes.text: Tabelog's remarks field for the Toyosu listing is a single sentence of local history: 「築地場内市場の大和寿司が豊洲市場に移転」.
It opened at Toyosu on 13 October 2018, two days after the market itself began trading.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog gives 大和寿司 at 江東区豊洲6-3-1 豊洲市場 5街区青果棟1F, coordinates 35.644785 / 139.786043, 112 m from Shijō-mae on the Yurikamome, 26 counter-only seats, 06:00-13:00 Monday to Saturday with Sundays, holidays and market closed days off, budget ¥6,000-7,999, cards / IC / iD / PayPay accepted, all-non-smoking, sake served, 魚料理にこだわる and 朝食・モーニングあり, opened 13 October 2018, and both the relocation note 「このお店は「中央区築地5-2-1」から移転しています」 and the remark 「築地場内市場の大和寿司が豊洲市場に移転」.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 26-seat market counter running one omakase for everyone, with no published allergen information and no wheat-free claim.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Nikiri — a wheat soy-sauce reduction — is brushed on each piece by the chef; no tamari is named.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish throughout; no vegetarian course exists.

positives.text: Takes cards, transport IC, iD and PayPay — unusually easy for a market counter, and one less thing to arrange in Japanese.

cultural_comfort.note: A market breakfast: Yurikamome to Shijō-mae, then the produce building's ground floor, any morning the market is open (Sundays, holidays and irregular Wednesdays are out — check the Toyosu calendar). Doors at 06:00, last orders by 13:00, and a queue at the wide 26-seat counter. Cards and PayPay are accepted, which makes it gentler than its neighbour 寿司大. Foreign visitors are entirely routine, but there is no menu and no lingering; you sit, you eat what comes, you leave.

enrich_note: RELOCATED, NOT MISLOCATED. 大和寿司 is real and open, but it left Tsukiji with the market: Tabelog states 「このお店は「中央区築地5-2-1」から移転しています」, gives the current address as 江東区豊洲6-3-1 inside Toyosu Market's block 5, an opening date of 13 October 2018, and the remark 「築地場内市場の大和寿司が豊洲市場に移転」.
